summary: CNAME chaining in split-horizon DNS causes OCSP to resolve via public egress and breaks mTLS/auth for private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
BrightCart reported production traffic on their Private (VPCE) deployment intermittently failing control-plane authenticated calls and model shard downloads. Failures correlate with OCSP lookups for certificate validation resolving to public internet addresses instead of internal OCSP responder IPs because of a CNAME chain that crosses split-horizon zones. Impact:
- Control-plane authentication attempts (mTLS) intermittently fail with certificate revocation lookup timeouts and fallbacks.
- Serving node artifact fetches return 502/403 when OCSP queries go out via customer internet egress instead of private resolver.
- Customer observed elevated retry/backoff and increased latency during peak jobs.
Environment:
- BrightCart private deployment (VPCE endpoint, us-east-1)
- Route53 split-horizon DNS with internal zone for redwood-internal.example & public zone for example.com
- Corporate egress via forwarder/proxy with strict outbound ACLs
- Redwood control-plane and serving nodes use internal resolver in VPC by default
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From a serving node in BrightCart's private deployment, initiate a model shard fetch that requires validation of the presigned URL certificate (internal CA).
2) Observe resolver behavior for ocsp.internal-ca.example -> CNAME ocsp.shared-ca.example -> public-ocsp-provider.com (public zone).

3) Note that the internal resolver returns the CNAME chain, but the split-horizon configuration lacks the matching public-to-private CNAME rewrite, causing final A records to resolve via public resolver paths on some nodes.

4) Reproduce intermittent failures by running concurrent shard fetches and ocsp queries; some queries route to public egress and get blocked by corporate ACLs or receive TTL/EDNS responses that cause timeouts.
observed_behavior: OCSP lookups intermittently time out or resolve to public IPs. mTLS certificate validation fails after OCSP timeout; control-plane auth retries and backoff occur. Artifact downloads either retry successfully (when internal path used) or fail with 502/403 when public path is chosen.
expected_behavior: Internal OCSP responder or private A records should be returned by the internal split-horizon zone for all serving/control-plane nodes so that OCSP and mTLS validations remain strictly internal and do not traverse corporate internet egress.
logs_and_snippets: Mar 13 11:22:01 serving-node kernel: resolver query: ocsp.internal-ca.example -> CNAME ocsp.shared-ca.example
Mar 13 11:22:01 serving-node network: DNS answer: ocsp.shared-ca.example -> A 54.23.11.9 (public) [via forwarder]
Mar 13 11:22:01 serving-node auth: ocsp fetch timeout after 5s; certificate validation failed; mTLS auth rejected
Mar 13 11:23:15 control-plane: artifact fetch returned 403 for shard 0001/128; presigned URL validated OCSP via public-ocsp-provider.com
investigation_notes: Customer provided pcap and dig traces showing CNAME chain crossing zone boundary (internal -> shared -> public).
Internal DNS config for redwood-internal.example only overrides direct names; it did not include wildcard or chained CNAMEs for ocsp.shared-ca.example.
We confirmed that nodes using the customer forwarder sometimes receive truncated EDNS responses which cause fallback to public resolver behaviors on some AZs.
Related ticket SUP-712345 noted earlier VPCE host-header mismatch; likely same customer's zone management workflow introduced a split-horizon gap during a recent PR.
mitigation_steps_taken: Suggested immediate customer-side workaround: create explicit internal A record for ocsp.shared-ca.example in the private hosted zone pointing at internal OCSP responder IPs.
On Redwood side: temporarily allow OCSP responder FQDN in our control-plane egress allowlist to avoid blocking when public resolution occurs (applied as short-lived emergency rule).
Advised BrightCart to add CNAME rewrite entries or avoid cross-zone CNAME chaining for security-sensitive endpoints.
Enabled additional DNS logging on serving nodes to track resolution path and flagged nodes that still saw public answers.
comments: 2026-03-13 12:05 - Aditi Rao (Support): Collected dig + pcap from customer; flagged as P1 due to production auth failures.
2026-03-13 13:20 - Michael Chen (SRE): Confirmed CNAME chain in traces. Recommending explicit internal A record as fastest fix. Opened PR to allowlist public-ocsp temporarily.
2026-03-13 15:10 - BrightCart (Customer Engineer): Added internal A record for ocsp.shared-ca.example per recommendation; reporting fewer failures but still seeing occasional timeouts.

2026-03-14 09:40 - Michael Chen (SRE): Found that forwarder EDNS truncation in us-east-1b causes fallback to system resolver on some nodes. Working with customer network team to fix forwarder settings.
2026-03-14 11:00 - Support (Aditi): Customer verified artifact downloads stable after internal A record + forwarder fix; monitoring for 24h then will request closure.
resolution: Workaround and permanent fix agreed: BrightCart added explicit internal A records for cross-zone OCSP hostnames and corrected their DNS forwarder EDNS/TC handling. Redwood rolled a temporary egress allowlist for the public OCSP hostname to reduce customer impact while DNS was corrected. Post-change validation (24h) shows no further mTLS or artifact failures. Follow-up action: update private deploy runbook to recommend avoiding CNAME chains that land in public zones for PKI/OCSP endpoints and add a DNS checklist for new customer zone rollouts.
follow_up_tasks: Add DNS CNAME-chain checks to onboarding checklist (owner: Solutions Engineering)
Create an automated alert for OCSP lookup paths that resolve outside private zones (owner: Observability)
Document recommended split-horizon patterns for OCSP/mTLS in confluence page linked above (owner: SRE)
